newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products - Gulf gasoline strong, but easing.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products - Gulf gasoline strong, but easing.

text.p: U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded gasoline differentials remained strong but gave up some of the day's sharp gains as the number of bids fell off by early Friday afternoon, traders said.
New York Harbor and Midcontinent gasoline differentials continued at higher levels in sympathy with Houston strength, while distillates showed mixed results in U.S. markets.

USG prompt "M1" grade unleaded, whose diffs had swelled 1.25 cents a gallon Friday morning ahead of a scheduling deadline for shipping product on the Houston-to-New York Colonial Pipleline, gave up about a half cent of the gains by midday, players said.
Although the Houston spot gasoline upswing helped push August NYMEX gasoline 0.60 cent higher at 59.20 cents by 1238 EDT/1638 GMT, a stronger 0.90-cent futures gain had been seen earlier Friday.
August heating oil was up just 0.14 cent at 52.25 cents a gallon early afternoon.
U.S. GULF

"Gasoline seems to be coming off a bit," one Gulf trader said, adding an "M1" parcel was sold early afternoon for 1.50 cents over August NYMEX, compared with the 2.0-cent-over deals done earlier in the day. An any-month "M1" parcel was heard sold for 1.25 cents under the August print.
One trader predicted Gulf gasoline diffs would retrace sharply in the next few weeks from what he termed "unsustainable" heights.

"Differentials in the Gulf historically have been about 2.75 cents below the near-month NYMEX screen this time of year, but are about 2.0 cents over now. It's getting overdone and can't last," the trader predicted.

Besides Colonial Pipeline scheduling, the reasons behind Friday's differential rally were not entirely clear. But players said demand appeared to be solid despite high output and that there appeared to be a speculative paper component behind the jump.

Other Gulf players said the fact traders were outnumbering refiners as buyers Friday morning buttressed a growing sense among players that someone was trying to bullishly influence the fate of an outstanding swap position.

Another backdrop to gasoline's strength was the outage due to a fire at a Mobil Corp hydrocracker at its Chalmette, Louisiana refinery, but traders cautioned that the crippling of the unit was not enough to singlehandedly move the market.
"It's just one of many factors," said another trader.
Indeed, prices have been firm all week long, traders said.

"It was kind of heading in that direction yesterday," said another trader, referring to M1 values of 0.75 cent over August NYMEX unleaded futures as of late Thursday -- a move of nearly 1.00 cent from differentials recorded from Wednesday.
MIDCONTINENT:

Gulf strength and strong demand helped widen differentials on Group Three conventional unleaded gasoline about a half cent a gallon by midday Friday, with barrels offered at about 3.85 cents over August futures, traders said.
"Inflation from the Gulf Coast is boosting the Group," one Group player said. "And there's lots of refiner and trading house buying here. Anybody who's anybody is buying."
Chicago conventional unleaded diffs were more steady, however, with offers at 2.75 cents over the print and any-month barrels pegged at 2.50 cents over.

Low sulfur diesel differentials, meanwhile, widened about 0.25 cent in both centers - with Group material offered at about 3.0 cents over August futures and Chicago product at 0.25 cents under the screen.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Strength in the U.S. Gulf helped firmed gasoline differentials in New York Harbor, where refiner and trader demand continued. Activity, however, was slightly subdued amid talk of more import cargoes than usual heading to the U.S.
"There appears to be more imports than usual but what's important is they won't arrive until the first half of August," said a Harbor trader.
"With the Gulf so tight, the chances are the barrels will be pulled into the south instead of the east coast," he added.
Much of Friday's focus centered on premium and reformulated gasoline, which has firmed due to tightness in MTBE and aromatics used to enhance octane.

Prompt "D2" 93-octane reformulated gasoline traded Friday morning at 7.75 cents over August futures, up about a quarter cent with sellers at midday at 8.00 cents. Regular "A2" 87-octane reformulated gasoline also firmed, with deals done at 0.75 cent over the print and sellers now at 1.00 cent.
"M1"-grade conventional unleaded was slightly weaker, with a deal done at 1.85 under the print.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1620
